title: Area and perimeter
summary: The [[perimeter|perimeter]] of a shape is the distance round its edge, and its [[area|area]] is the flat space inside. You find both for rectangles, triangles, [[parallelogram|parallelograms]] and [[trapezium|trapeziums]]. The key is always to use the [[perpendicular-height|perpendicular height]], never a slanting side.

goals.text: Work out the [[perimeter|perimeter]] of a shape, including one whose sides are algebraic expressions.
Work out the [[area|area]] of a rectangle, and of a shape made from rectangles.
Find the area of a parallelogram, triangle and trapezium using the [[perpendicular-height|perpendicular height]].
Work backwards from an area or a perimeter to a missing length.

before.prompt: Which quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
before.explain: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. Parallelograms and rectangles have two pairs. Revise it in {{lesson:4.1}}.

before.prompt: Two lines are [[perpendicular|perpendicular]]. What angle do they meet at, in degrees?
before.hint: Think of the corner of a square.
before.explain: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle: a quarter turn, $360 \div 4 = 90^{\circ}$. Revise it in {{lesson:4.1}}.

blocks.text: Imagine walking all the way round the edge of a field. The distance you walk is its [[perimeter|perimeter]]. It is a length, so it is measured in cm, m or km.

blocks.statement: The total length of the boundary of a flat shape.
blocks.plain: Add up the lengths of all the outside edges.

blocks.text: A rectangle has two equal lengths and two equal widths. So its perimeter is two lengths plus two widths.

For a triangle, a [[parallelogram|parallelogram]] or a [[trapezium|trapezium]], add every side. A parallelogram's opposite sides are equal, so you only need the lengths of two sides that meet at a corner.

blocks.question: A garden bed is a trapezium. Its parallel sides are $9\text{ m}$ and $5\text{ m}$, and its two slanting sides are both $4.5\text{ m}$. Work out the perimeter of the bed.

blocks.prompt: A parallelogram has sides of $13\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$. Work out its perimeter, in cm.
blocks.hint: It has two sides of each length.

blocks.text: Sides can be algebraic expressions. Add them in the same way, then collect the $x$ terms and the numbers separately.

blocks.question: A rectangle has length $(4x + 1)\text{ cm}$ and width $(x - 3)\text{ cm}$. Its perimeter is $56\text{ cm}$. Work out the length of the rectangle.
steps: Set it equal to 56: $10x - 4 = 56$. Add 4: $10x = 60$, so $x = 6$.
The length is $4 \times 6 + 1 = 25$. Check: the width is $6 - 3 = 3$, and $2(25 + 3) = 56$.

blocks.prompt: A triangle has sides $(2x + 5)\text{ cm}$, $(3x - 1)\text{ cm}$ and $(x + 4)\text{ cm}$. Which expression is its perimeter, in its simplest form?
blocks.hint: Add the three sides once each. Take care with the $-1$.
blocks.explain: $2x + 3x + x = 6x$ and $5 - 1 + 4 = 8$. A triangle's sides are each added once, so don't double them.

blocks.text: Adding one length and one width of a rectangle, which gives only half the perimeter. Double it, or write $2l + 2w$ from the start.
[[area|Area]] counts how many unit squares cover a shape. A square $1\text{ cm}$ by $1\text{ cm}$ has an area of $1\text{ cm}^{2}$, said "one square centimetre".

blocks.statement: The amount of flat surface inside a shape, measured in square units such as $\text{cm}^{2}$ or $\text{m}^{2}$.
blocks.plain: How many unit squares it takes to cover the shape.

blocks.text: A rectangle $5\text{ cm}$ long and $3\text{ cm}$ wide holds 3 rows of 5 squares. That is $3 \times 5 = 15\text{ cm}^{2}$, so area is length times width.
For a shape made of rectangles, split it into rectangles and add their areas. Find any missing side by adding or subtracting the sides you know.

blocks.alt: An L-shaped floor plan with all corners right angles. The bottom edge is 9 m and the left edge is 7 m. The top edge is 5 m. The lower right edge is 4 m. A rectangle is missing from the top right corner, so the two edges of the step are not labelled. A dashed line splits the shape into a tall rectangle on the left and a short one on the right.

blocks.question: The figure shows the floor of a room. All its corners are right angles. Work out the area of the floor.
steps: Split along the dashed line. The left rectangle is $5\text{ m}$ wide and $7\text{ m}$ tall: $5 \times 7 = 35$.
The right rectangle is $9 - 5 = 4\text{ m}$ wide and $4\text{ m}$ tall: $4 \times 4 = 16$.
Check another way: the full $9$ by $7$ rectangle is $63$. The missing corner is $4$ by $7 - 4 = 3$, which is $12$. $63 - 12 = 51$.

blocks.prompt: Work out the perimeter of the floor in the figure, in metres.
blocks.hint: The step has a horizontal edge of $9 - 5$ and a vertical edge of $7 - 4$.
blocks.explain: The missing edges are $4\text{ m}$ and $3\text{ m}$. So $9 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 32\text{ m}$.

blocks.text: A [[parallelogram|parallelogram]] leans over. Cut the triangle off one end and slide it to the other end. The shape becomes a rectangle with the same base and the same area.

blocks.alt: A parallelogram with base b along the bottom and a dashed perpendicular height h drawn from the top left corner straight down to the base, with a right-angle mark. The right-angled triangle to the left of the height is shaded. An arrow shows it sliding to the right end, where a dashed copy fills the gap and turns the parallelogram into a rectangle with base b and height h.

blocks.text: The rectangle's height is the distance straight up from the base, at right angles to it. This is the [[perpendicular-height|perpendicular height]], not the slanting side.

blocks.statement: The distance from the base to the opposite side or corner, measured at right angles to the base.
blocks.plain: Straight up from the base, never along a slanting side.

blocks.question: A parallelogram has a base of $11\text{ cm}$ and slanting sides of $6.5\text{ cm}$. Its perpendicular height is $5\text{ cm}$. Work out its area.
steps: Pick out the base and the perpendicular height: $b = 11$ and $h = 5$. The slanting side, $6.5$, is not needed.
$A = 55$, in square centimetres. The height is shorter than the slanting side, as it must be.

blocks.prompt: A parallelogram has base $14\text{ cm}$, slanting sides of $9\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $7\text{ cm}$. What is its area?
blocks.hint: Which two lengths meet at a right angle?
blocks.explain: $14 \times 7 = 98$. Using the slanting side gives $126$, and halving gives $49$, which is a triangle's area.

blocks.text: Giving an area in cm instead of $\text{cm}^{2}$. Perimeter is a length; area is always in square units.

Take any triangle and a copy of it turned upside down. The two fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and the same [[perpendicular-height|perpendicular height]]. So the triangle's [[area|area]] is half of $bh$.

blocks.alt: Two diagrams. On the left, a shaded triangle with base b and a dashed perpendicular height h, joined to an unshaded copy turned upside down. Together they make a parallelogram with base b and height h, so the triangle is half of it. On the right, a shaded trapezium with parallel sides a on top and b at the bottom and dashed height h, joined to an unshaded copy turned upside down. Together they make a parallelogram whose base is a plus b and whose height is h, so the trapezium is half of it.

blocks.text: The triangle formula is on the exam formula list. The other area formulas in this lesson are not, so learn them.
In a [[right-angled-triangle|right-angled triangle]], the two shorter sides meet at the right angle. So they are a base and its perpendicular height. The longest side slants.

blocks.question: A sail is a right-angled triangle with sides $2.4\text{ m}$, $7\text{ m}$ and $7.4\text{ m}$. Work out the area of the sail.
steps: The longest side, $7.4$, is opposite the right angle and slants. The other two sides meet at the right angle.
Without a calculator: $2.4 \times 7 = 16.8$, and half of $16.8$ is $8.4$.

blocks.prompt: A triangle has an area of $42\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a base of $12\text{ cm}$. Work out its perpendicular height, in cm.
blocks.explain: Half of 12 is 6, so $6h = 42$ and $h = 42 \div 6 = 7\text{ cm}$.

blocks.text: Forgetting the $\frac{1}{2}$ in a triangle's area, which doubles the answer. Base times height is the whole parallelogram.

A [[trapezium|trapezium]] has one pair of [[parallel|parallel]] sides, $a$ and $b$. A copy turned upside down fits on to make a parallelogram with base $a + b$ and height $h$. The trapezium is half of it.

blocks.prompt: A trapezium has parallel sides of $6\text{ cm}$ and $14\text{ cm}$. The perpendicular height between them is $4\text{ cm}$, and one slanting side is $5\text{ cm}$. What is its area?
blocks.hint: Only the parallel sides and the perpendicular height go in the formula.
blocks.explain: $\frac{1}{2}(6 + 14) \times 4 = 10 \times 4 = 40$. Using the slanting side gives $50$; forgetting the half gives $80$.

blocks.question: A trapezium has an area of $54\text{ cm}^{2}$. The two parallel sides measure $7\text{ cm}$ and $x\text{ cm}$, and they are $6\text{ cm}$ apart. Find $x$.
steps: The distance between parallel sides is measured at right angles, so $h = 6$.

blocks.text: "Work out the area": write the formula with your numbers in, such as $\frac{1}{2}(7 + 11) \times 6$. That line earns the method mark even if your arithmetic slips.
Perimeter is a length (cm, m). Area is in square units ($\text{cm}^{2}$, $\text{m}^{2}$).
Every area formula uses the perpendicular height, at right angles to the base. A slanting side is never the height.
Only the triangle formula is on the formula list. Learn the rectangle, parallelogram and trapezium formulas.
Shapes made of rectangles: split them up, and find missing sides by adding or subtracting.

mistakes: Forgetting the half in the triangle or trapezium formula, which doubles the area.
Using a slanting side as the height. Use the length that meets the base at a right angle.
Taking the longest side of a right-angled triangle as its height. Use the two shorter sides, which meet at the right angle.
Adding a rectangle's length and width only once, which gives half the perimeter.
Putting a slanting side of a trapezium into $a + b$. Only the two parallel sides go there.
Sign slips when collecting terms in a perimeter expression. Collect the numbers on their own, with their signs.
examTips: "Give your answer in its simplest form" for a perimeter: collect the $x$ terms and the numbers into one expression such as $10x - 4$.
On Paper 1 and Paper 2, set the arithmetic out by hand: halve the even number first, such as $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 = 6$, then multiply.
Read which lengths a diagram gives. A diagram marked NOT TO SCALE must not be measured, and it may show a slanting length you don't need.
Write units on your answer if the answer line has none: cm for perimeter, $\text{cm}^{2}$ for area.
